verdict.reason: Every element of the finding checks out in the repo. Doc.mergeBlocks (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:379-389) now performs two store writes: store.mergeBlock then, when a boolean flag is stranded, dropStaleStyleOff -> writeStaleStyleOffEdits -> store.applyStyles (document.ts:481-485, 569-575). Under the production store these are two separate undo units: YorkieDocStore.snapshot() is an explicit no-op (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2727-2729), mergeBlock opens its own doc.update() (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2275) and applyStyles opens another (yorkie-doc-store.ts:1806); a grep for batch/pause/group/transaction in that file found no grouping seam. The docs editor uses this store in production (docs-view.tsx:322). Callers outside the diff each stage exactly one saveSnapshot() per keystroke and assume the merge is one write (text-editor.ts:1937 handleBackspace -> document.ts:320; also text-editor.ts:1959, 1988/2005, 2030, 2037/2051, 2058/2076, 3243/3345/3411). The path is reachable because heading-6 supplies italic: true (named-styles.ts:91), so styleOffAsClear legitimately stores italic:false in a Heading 6 run and collectStaleStyleOff emits a patch once that run lands in a paragraph. The PR's own comment at view/editor.ts:1049-1057 concedes exactly this two-Cmd+Z hazard for named-style changes and says the batch() seam needed to fold the writes does not exist yet. This is a cross-module invariant (one keystroke = one undo unit) relied on by callers and by the undo implementation, both outside the diff, so it is in the blast-radius lane at major impact. The identical pre-existing pattern in setBlockType (document.ts:613-618) is not a guard and does not make the finding unreachable, and 'pre-existing' is not a refutation ground.

finding.summary: Internal table-cell paste bypasses the new `dropStaleStyleOffAll` cleanup
finding.evidence: `handleNativePaste` runs the cleanup only on the `data.blocks` branch (text-editor.ts:1258-1264). The sibling branch at text-editor.ts:1247-1253 (`data.tableCells` → `this.pasteTableCells(data.tableCells)`) comes from the same internal WAFFLEDOCS_MIME clipboard payload and `pasteTableCells` clones the cells verbatim (`cloneTableCells`, text-editor.ts:3743), so runs copied out of a Heading 6 keep their explicit `italic: false` and land in cell paragraphs whose named style never supplies italic — exactly the dead flag the diff's paste-path comment says the cleanup exists to remove. Fix belongs on the new code (add the same `dropStaleStyleOffAll()` call to the tableCells branch).

verdict.reason: Verified directly: the internal-clipboard `data.tableCells` branch (text-editor.ts:1247-1253) returns without any stale-style sweep, while its sibling `data.blocks` branch calls `this.doc.dropStaleStyleOffAll()` (text-editor.ts:1264). Tracing everything `pasteTableCells` (text-editor.ts:3725-3793) invokes — `cloneTableCells`, `normalizeTableMerges`, `Doc.insertBlockAt` (document.ts:648-651), `Doc.updateBlockDirect` (document.ts:640-643) — none performs the cleanup; those model methods only write to the store and `refresh()`. A repo-wide grep for `dropStaleStyleOff*` returns only four production call sites (document.ts:388, document.ts:618, text-editor.ts:1264, editor.ts:1063), none on the cell-paste path, so no counterexample exists. `italic: false` does survive the payload round trip (`sanitizeInlineStyle`, clipboard.ts:134-140), so the flag can reach that branch. The reviewer's stated mechanism is partly inaccurate — `cloneTableCells` (clipboard.ts:389-394) and `sanitizeBlock` (clipboard.ts:301-332) preserve `type`/`headingLevel` and `pasteTableCells` replaces whole cells (text-editor.ts:3744, 3776) rather than splicing runs into a foreign-typed block, so in the common same-doc case the run lands back in a Heading 6 and the `false` stays a live override (blockStyleId, named-styles.ts:105-110). But staleness is still reachable: copy cells, redefine Heading 6 via a named-style entry point (whose sweep at editor.ts:1063 cannot touch a clipboard payload), then paste; or paste into a doc with a divergent style table. Since the missing call is real and a reachable path strands the flag, I cannot produce a refutation; confidence is low only because the harm window is narrower than the finding describes.

finding.evidence: `mergeBlocks` (document.ts:379-382) calls `store.mergeBlock` + `refresh()` with no stale-flag cleanup, while `setBlockType` (document.ts:604-611) was given one. Backspace at the start of a Heading 6 merges its runs (which legitimately carry `italic: false` because the heading style supplies italic — see the diff's own test at test/model/document.test.ts:353) into the previous paragraph, where nothing supplies italic. The flag is then dead exactly as after a block-type change, blocks re-merging in `normalizeInlines`, and pins the run against later style redefinition. `deleteBackward` (document.ts:320) reaches this on the hottest editing path.

verdict.reason: The finding is an absence claim: that `Doc.mergeBlocks` performs `store.mergeBlock` + `refresh()` with no stale-`false` cleanup, unlike `setBlockType`. Reading the actual method refutes this. `mergeBlocks` spans document.ts:379-389, not 379-382 as quoted, and line 388 is `if (this.dropStaleStyleOff(blockId)) this.refresh();` — precisely the sweep said to be missing, and the same call `setBlockType` uses at document.ts:618. The comment at document.ts:382-387 spells out the exact Heading-6-merged-into-paragraph `italic: false` scenario the finding describes as unhandled. Ordering is sound: `refresh()` at line 381 precedes the sweep, so `dropStaleStyleOff` -> `findBlock(blockId)` (document.ts:481-485) inspects the post-merge block where the stranded runs now reside, and a second `refresh()` fires only if edits were written. The `deleteBackward` path cited as the hot bypass (document.ts:320) calls this same `mergeBlocks`, so it is covered rather than bypassing. The reviewer's greps missed the call because it sits just past the line range they read; `.agent-review/security/summary.md:6` independently describes `dropStaleStyleOff(blockId)` as present in `mergeBlocks`.

finding.summary: The cleanup write is a second Yorkie undo unit, so block-type change / style redefinition / paste now need two Cmd+Z
finding.evidence: `YorkieDocStore.snapshot()` is a no-op — "Yorkie tracks undo units via doc.update()" (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2727-2729) — and `applyStyles` opens its own `this.doc.update(...)` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:1806). `Doc.setBlockType` now issues `store.setBlockType` (one update) followed by `dropStaleStyleOff` → `store.applyStyles` (a second update); `afterNamedStyleChange` (view/editor.ts:1052) does the same after `writeStylesAndRematerialize` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2686, itself documented as "a single doc.update so the whole change is one undo unit"); the paste path does it after `insertBlocks`. The new comments claim the cleanup "undoes as one step" with the caller, which holds only for `MemDocStore`'s snapshot stack — under the collaborative store the first Cmd+Z undoes only the cleanup and leaves the heading/redefinition/paste in place.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. YorkieDocStore.snapshot() is a no-op (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2727-2729) and undo() pops exactly one Yorkie unit (2731-2736); applyStyles opens its own doc.update (1806) and writeStylesAndRematerialize opens a separate one (2710). Doc.setBlockType issues store.setBlockType then dropStaleStyleOff -> store.applyStyles (document.ts:613-618, 573), Doc.mergeBlocks does the same (document.ts:380-388, reachable from the backspace/merge paths at text-editor.ts:1959/2005/2030/2076/3243/3345/3411), afterNamedStyleChange sweeps after the registry write (editor.ts:1063, callers 2847/2877/2882/2887), and the internal-clipboard paste sweeps after insertBlocks (text-editor.ts:1256-1264). There is no batch()/coalescing seam on DocStore (store.ts:85-90), so under the collaborative store the first Cmd+Z reverts only the cleanup. This is a cross-package invariant break ("one user action = one undo unit") invisible in the diff — in the blast-radius lane, major impact. The finding's only inaccuracy is its paraphrase of the comments: editor.ts:1051-1057 actually admits the two-Cmd+Z behaviour and calls a batch() seam a follow-up, rather than claiming one-step undo. That acknowledgment covers only the named-style path and is a comment, not a guard, so it does not make setBlockType/mergeBlocks/paste unreachable or already-guarded. No named refutation ground applies.
